html:
The ongoing war with Iran continues to be the dominant global development, with President Trump issuing conflicting statements about its trajectory while international bodies and major banks highlight its wide-ranging impact.

US Politics & Media: Trump has banned CNN, MS Now, and Politico from the White House, citing "fake news" and threatening to extend the restriction to more outlets. This action follows a history of a tense relationship with the media. Separately, a federal judge has ruled that Trump cannot demolish the Kennedy Center without prior notice.

Iran War & Middle East Security: The conflict with Iran remains a central global concern, with President Trump stating that the U.S. is "hopefully toward the end" of the war and planning talks with Gulf leaders, while also reportedly weighing renewed major attacks. The U.S. House of Representatives has voted for a third time to end the war. This comes as the UN has found grounds to believe the U.S. committed war crimes in Iran, and Russia and China vetoed a U.S. proposal for UN experts to monitor sanctions on Iran. In the region, Houthi forces have tightened their grip on Yemen's Red Sea coast and the Bab el Mandeb, extending their reach and threatening Saudi oil exports, with one person killed by an intercepted Houthi drone in Saudi Arabia. Iran claims it struck an oil tanker in the Strait of Hormuz, while the U.S. has approved a potential $24.3 billion sale of F-35 jets to Saudi Arabia, a move that Hebrew media reports indicate Tel Aviv fears.

Great Power Dynamics & AI: Amid regional conflicts, great powers are also navigating the rise of artificial intelligence. Trump and Xi are expected to discuss AI, with informal "Track Two" talks already underway. A false alert generated by AI nearly led the U.S. military to raid a Chinese ship in the Middle East. Europe, meanwhile, faces a dilemma over AI safety, weighing the choice between embracing the technology and risking dependency on U.S. and Chinese tools, or shunning it and losing out on growth.

Russia-Ukraine & European Security: Russian hybrid attacks against Europe are intensifying, with French president Macron tasking his government to protect critical infrastructure. Polish Prime Minister Donald Tusk warned of potential "accidental" Russian attacks on Ukraine's allies, asserting that such strikes aim to paralyze NATO. As Russia holds parliamentary elections amid reports of war fatigue, its drone efforts in Ukraine appear to be stalling, though they pose a threat to Western officials traveling to Kyiv. Canada is also exploring "associate member" status in the European Union, separate from Washington.

Global Economy & Markets: The war with Iran is deeply impacting global energy markets, with J.P. Morgan struggling to forecast oil prices due to Trump's actions and assuming economic "red lines" the U.S. would be unwilling to cross. While oil futures have fallen for a third day on easing supply concerns, Houthi attacks continue to threaten Saudi oil and have pushed up global fuel prices. Trump has also demanded a rapid reduction in interest rates in the United States.

Regional Conflicts & Humanitarian Concerns: A vehicle loaded with explosives rammed a mosque in Pakistan, killing at least 21 people, including a four-year-old child, and gunmen also opened fire on a police facility. In Nigeria, dozens of suspected illegal miners died in custody, with authorities linking the deaths to disease, a claim disputed by intelligence reports and relatives. Fighting in Yemen has displaced 112,000 people, with thousands fleeing to Djibouti. In the Levant, the Israeli army set fire to a hospital in Mais al-Jabal, Lebanon, which the Health Ministry denounced as a "moral failure," and a Palestinian was killed in an Israeli strike on a motorcycle in Gaza City.
